FM04.reasoning: Missing values are imputed using group-level modes computed over the combined train and test datasets, leaking test set information into the training data.

FM15.reasoning: The agent relies entirely on accuracy for model evaluation and threshold tuning without checking if the classes are balanced or if the metric is robust.

other_failure_modes.name: Feature engineering leakage
other_failure_modes.description: Aggregating features or computing frequency encodings on a concatenated dataframe of train and test sets leaks test distribution information into the training data.

other_failure_modes.name: Ineffective categorical imputation
other_failure_modes.description: Casting a pandas column to string before calling `fillna` converts actual NaN values into the string 'nan', which causes the subsequent `fillna` to do nothing.

summary: The solution implements a solid CatBoost model with extensive feature engineering and a robust cross-validation scheme. However, it suffers from severe data leakage because the train and test sets are combined before computing group-level imputations and aggregate features, allowing test set information to contaminate the training data. Additionally, there is a minor logic bug where categorical missing values are improperly handled due to string casting before imputation.
